review.scope: Full-site PUBLIC static regression budget: all 499 generated pages from a sanitized build, inspected against actual Chromium axe findings. Not WCAG conformance and not owner acceptance of these defects.
review.backlog: 14694 existing node findings on 499 of 499 pages. By impact: {'moderate': 11227, 'serious': 3436, 'critical': 30, 'minor': 1}. Top rules: 10046 region, 3251 color-contrast, 485 landmark-one-main, 344 landmark-unique, 220 landmark-no-duplicate-contentinfo, 142 link-in-text-block. About 11,000 are structural and come from shared page templates (content outside landmarks, missing main, duplicate or unlabeled landmarks); fixing the shared shell removes most. Critical findings are unlabeled form fields and meta-refresh. No image-alt findings were observed. Repair source templates with their owners, remove resolved entries, never add entries to hide a new finding. No rule exclusions.
review.matching: Exact page, rule, selector and failure message. A page not listed here fails on any finding. Resolved entries and pages no longer generated must be pruned. Page clock frozen to 2026-01-15 12:00 Honolulu; each page settles 1.5s and must give two identical axe results in a row (live-clock pages otherwise flake). No automatic baseline update: use `npm run scan:propose`, inspect .work/proposed-baseline.json, then copy it deliberately. Exception, documented 2026-11-17: for the target-size rule only, measured pixel values inside the message are ignored (they follow runner fallback-font metrics and changed between two identical GitHub runs); page, rule, selector and the rest of the message must still match.
review.limitations: Desktop 1280x900 initial static rendered state only, no backend, remote resources, interaction, keyboard/screen-reader or manual WCAG checks. axe 'incomplete' nodes (about 46,000) need human review and are not counted as passes. Data-regenerated pages (for example seed_reports donor pages) may need a re-proposal when their data changes; see docs/CI_OWNER_ACTIONS.md section 3B.
review.platform: 2026-11-17: the gate runs on the GitHub ubuntu runner, which is the authoritative platform. The baseline was first captured on Windows and then reconciled shard by shard to the first Linux runs. Findings that depend on font metrics (inline-link target-size, tag contrast) or on overflow handling (keyboard-unfocusable scrollable tables) differ by a handful of entries between the two. A local Windows scan can therefore report a few differences that CI does not.
